metadata.notes: Input pasted in chat; no source IDs, so REQ/AC/BR IDs are assigned.

evidence: Labelled 'Requirement:' with a single 'should be able to' statement for one feature
Numbered 'Acceptance Criteria' list 1-6 attached to that requirement
No story format ('As a...'), no document sections, no API or UI artefacts

requirements.text: A logged-in user can add an available product to the shopping cart from the product details page

preconditions: User is on a product details page
error_conditions: Product is out of stock (AC 5, AC 6)

acceptance_criteria.text: User can click the 'Add to Cart' button
The selected product is added to the cart
Product name, price and quantity are displayed correctly in the cart
Out-of-stock products cannot be added to the cart
User sees an appropriate message when adding an out-of-stock product

business_rules.text: Adding to cart is specified for logged-in users only

clarifications.question: Is there a quantity selector on the product details page, or does each 'Add to Cart' click add exactly 1 unit?
clarifications.why: AC 4 mentions quantity but no way to choose it; quantity validation and limits cannot be tested without this.

clarifications.question: When a product already in the cart is added again, does its quantity increase, or is a new line created? Does the cart count show total units or distinct products?
clarifications.why: Changes the expected result of AC 3 for repeat adds.

clarifications.question: What is the exact out-of-stock message text?
What happens when a user who is not logged in clicks 'Add to Cart' (redirect to login, guest cart, or button hidden)?
clarifications.why: The requirement covers logged-in users only; guest behaviour is undefined.

assumptions.text: Each 'Add to Cart' click adds a quantity of 1 (no quantity selector is described).
Adding a product that is already in the cart increases the cart count by 1 and its total quantity in the cart to 2 (line structure is not asserted).
The out-of-stock message states that the product is out of stock or unavailable; exact wording is not asserted.
